text.tspan: Page 16, Code is already a graph
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“this idea of "fractal semantic graphs" is a
good example that should make the reader
think & ideally make a paradigm shift [and]
Focus here and explain it”
Fractal semantic graphs is the idea that can shift the
reader's thinking: focus the chapter on it and explain it.
DRAW IT
“visualise this”
Draw the layers: a law in a graph of laws, an article in a
graph of terms.
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck: The newsroom's introduction to
what I call]”
Say the idea without its provenance.
WHAT WORKS, KEEP IT
“this is a good way to start explaining
graphs → connections”
'The world is made of connections; groups of groups are
how we think' is a good way into graphs.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“find better word [under: finding]”
'A chain that ends in a rumour is a finding too' needs a
better word than finding.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“define better [circled: A refactor is]”
Define refactor better, for a reader who has not met the
word.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“rewrite [the newsroom example struck]”
Rewrite the honest answer on AI-generated code; cut the
newsroom's sgit example.
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“good but for later in the book since most
ZX founders have no idea what we are talking
about here ↳ on this topic see what we did
at secrets.sgit.ai”
Code is already a graph is good, but it belongs later:
most ZX founders will not follow it on page 16. See
secrets.sgit.ai for the topic.
